verdict:
# K.16804 and Gilgameš Tablet V: no plausible fit

## 1. What the fragment preserves

**Column 1'** holds only line-endings: `[...] x`, `[... m]ar/r]ad`, `[... li]l`, `[...] x`. These are too little to match anything. There is no divine determinative and no recognisable word.

**Column 2'** holds line-beginnings, with several indented lines (`$___$`):

| Line | Signs | Normalisation / sense |
|---|---|---|
| 2' | (indented) `mam#-ma [...]` | *mamma*, "anyone" |
| 3' | `ba-tu-la ša₂ ina s[u-un ...]` | *batūla ša ina sūn…*, "the youth who in the lap of…" (the file note cites BWL 260) |
| 4' | `aš₂-la šu-uš-lu-[ša ...]` | *ašla šušluša*, "a three-ply rope" (accusative) |
| 5' | (indented) `ina/bi UGU/ka aš₂?# [...]` | unclear |
| 6' | `ar-da-t[u ...]` | *ardatu*, "young woman" |
| 7'–9' | `ta-[...]`, `qa-x [...]`, `x [...]` | too broken to use |

## 2. The only point of contact

Line 4' clearly echoes Tablet V line 79, *ašlu šušlušu* ("a three-ply rope [is not easily broken]"). This is part of Enkidu's string of sayings about the strength of two (V 75–81). It is therefore the only candidate location to test.

## 3. Testing V 76–81 against column 2'

Nineveh manuscript NinNA1a ii 21–26 preserves this stretch:

| Tablet V | NinNA1a | Fragment | Match? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 76 | `[2] lu-ba-ra-tu-ma` | 2' `mam-ma` | No |
| 77 | `[lu m]uš-hal-ṣi-tum₃-ma` | — | — |
| 78 | `[ši]t-ta taš-ka-a-ta` | 3' `ba-tu-la ša₂ ina s[u-un` | No |
| 79 | `x aš₂-lu šu-uš-lu-šu₂` | 4' `aš₂-la šu-uš-lu-[ša` | Wording yes, form no |
| 80 | `[1 UR.G]I₇ dan-nu 2 mi-ra-[nu-šu₂` | 5' `ina/bi UGU/ka aš₂?` | No |
| 81 | `[iš-da]-a-ka ki-i[n-ma` | 6' `ar-da-t[u` | No |

The mismatches are decisive for four reasons:

- **The lines on either side do not match.** The line before the rope saying should be *šittā takšāti* ("two triplets"), not *batūla ša ina sūn…*. The line after should be *ištēn kalbu dannu* ("one strong dog"), not the fragment's reading *ina/bi UGU/ka aš*. No other gap in Tablet V offers a *batūlu … ardatu* sequence either.
- **The case ending differs.** All Tablet V witnesses write the nominative *aš-lu* (NinNA1a, BabNB1, BabaNB1). The fragment has the accusative *aš-la šušluša*, which implies a different syntactic frame.
- **The vocabulary is foreign to this episode.** *Batūlu* ("youth") and *ardatu* ("young woman") belong to a different register. That pairing, with a *sūnu* ("lap") clause, is typical of proverb and wisdom collections. The file note's cross-reference to BWL 260, in Lambert's collection of Babylonian proverbs, points the same way.
- **The layout is wrong.** The fragment has frequent indented continuation lines and short line units. This does not correspond to the line division of the Kuyunjik Gilgameš manuscripts at V 76–81.

## 4. Conclusion

K.16804 does **not** belong to Tablet V. It is best explained as a fragment of a **proverb or wisdom collection** that quotes the widespread saying about the three-ply rope, the same saying Enkidu uses at V 79 (compare also Ecclesiastes 4:12). Its note "Cf. Gilg V" marks a parallel in wording, not a join or duplicate. The fragment should not be used to restore any line of Tablet V.
